rationale: This is a sociolinguistics and critical discourse analysis study examining workplace frame conflicts, code-switching, and linguistic inequality in employee/customer conversations. The partly state-owned enterprise supplying water, sewage treatment, and waste collection in Galicia is merely the workplace recording venue; the study does not examine household or community water/sanitation service access (C1), any legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism governing service access (C2), or any water/sanitation access outcome (C4). Excluded under E01 (non-water/sanitation sociolinguistic topic; incidental site mention).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both readings yield exclude: although the interviews were recorded at a partly state-owned water, sewage, and waste enterprise and contrast local communicative patterns with professionals' institutional discursive style, the study is a sociolinguistic analysis of workplace code-switching and conversational frame conflict with no institutional/legal mechanism governing service delivery and no water or sanitation access outcome.

evidence_quotes.quote: Frame conflict and social inequality in the workplace: professional and local discourse struggles in employee/customer interactions
Specifically, I analyse the frame conflicts that arise when customers mobilize local discursive patterns, code-switching and conversational topics.
The research is based on employee/customer interviews recorded at a partly state-owned enterprise that supplies water, sewage treatment and waste collection in a borough in Galicia (Spain).
